newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest bourse's BUX ends at new closing high.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bourse's BUX ends at new closing high.

text.p: The Hungarian bourse joined record-breaking European markets on Wednesday responding to upbeat comments by U.S. Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan and to a strong dollar with a new closing high, traders said.
The BUX index finished at a preliminary 7,503.73 points, up 64.64. At one point, the BUX also hit a new trading high of 7,549.43 points.
"People had predicted a strong rise for today as a cumulative impact of the extremely strong dollar, Greenspan and gains on European markets," said Gyorgy Czipo of ING Barings.
"This more or less materialised but in some cases the rise remained below what could have been expected."

Oil company MOL and chemicals company TVK hardly benefited from the overall surge, with MOL adding only 25 forints to finish at 4,295 and TVK dipping five forints to 3,920. OTP fell 200 forints to 6,400.
Hotel firm Danubius firmed 410 forints to end at 6,200 forints, a level Czipo said was "pretty realistic," but added trading centred between 5,950 and 6,000 forints.
"Investors are trying to find stocks...which benefited less from the market's recent surge," Czipo said, adding there were not any new corporate developments around Danubius to help its price.
Rabobank Investment Ltd started coverage on Wednesday of Danubius with a 'buy' and of TVK with a 'hold' recommendation.

Robert Feuer, analyst at WestMerchant in London, expected a sideways trend for most of the market until the release of the first half earnings, the deadline for which is August 15, but added that some might outperform in the next two weeks or so.
"Tile manufacturer Zalakeramia might rise as new buyers appeared on its markets," Feuer said.

"I also think of (plastics firm) Pannonplast as a potential gainer because Pannonplast is in strong correlation with (home improvement product maker) Graboplast and...there's a significant difference between their prices."
Probable good first half earnings will help Pannonplast to catch up with Graboplast, he added.
On Wednesday both hit new highs, Graboplast at 11,900 forints and Pannonplast at 10,400, Feuer said.
